actions._charges(ref=).why: actions._charges computes reachable_paths(actor, speed(world, actor, {"charge": True}), kind="charge") ONCE, above the per-swing loop, so the ctx carries no ref and a gate on "a charge made with this named row" has nothing to read. The row's note names a SECOND, unsymbolled gap: "increases TO 8" replaces the speed and c.bonus("speed") only adds.

actions._picking_up(cost=).why: Cast.grant_action(what, cost) + actions.GRANTABLE + query.granted_actions is exactly the mechanism. Two blockers: "pick_up" is not a GRANTABLE word and _picking_up writes cost = MINOR as a constant; and the readers UNION the granted cost with the printed one, so it can only make an action cheaper -- which is the row's own stated point.

actions.aid_defence(requires=bloodied).why: c.grant_action is a plain bonus carrier with no predicate field, and the ally is not chosen until actions.perform runs cast.choose, so at offer time there is no ally to test

actions.bluff().why: The check rolls -- f2092 and p16677 both make one -- but actions.legal offers no bluff-for-advantage standard action, so there is nothing to intercept and no beneficiary to redirect.

actions.call_companion().why: Cast.recast(ref, *, action, per_turn, until), read by actions._recasts: the row keeps its own menu entry and gains a second at the cheaper price, and per_turn=1 is "once during that turn". The summon is a declared row -- p6515, action=MINOR, requires=_no_spirit -- so p6515's own Requirement supplies the "only while the spirit is away" half, which _recasts honours via usable().

actions.familiar_switch.why: Switching a familiar's mode is a Cast verb with NO ENTRY in actions.legal, so "a free action instead of a minor" has nothing to cheapen; c.grant_action raises on a word no reader looks for (#762). Wants an action-menu entry in engine/actions.py plus the word in GRANTABLE.

actions.legal('ready').why: `actions.legal` offers powers, recasts, instinctives, commands, charges, hiding, picking up and spending, and there is no `ready` kind anywhere in the module. m855a2's bonus has no readied attack to sit on because readying is not an action a creature can take.

actions.legal('reload').why: c.grant_action states its whole vocabulary and says anything else is carried, costs nothing and does nothing

actions.legal(free_despite_stun=).why: A one-condition waiver already exists and is used by can_react for exactly this printed shape; `legal` calls can_act without it. Not run down: where a per-creature waiver would be stored so legal can read it, and how to limit the carve-out to free-cost actions.

actions.move_grabbed().why: actions.legal offers bull_rush/grab/aid_attack/aid_defence and nothing for a captive, so the relaxation has no manoeuvre to relax

actions.move_in_zone().why: c.grant_action(what, cost, squares_=) is the mechanism and actions.GRANTABLE already carries shift and move_zone -- c.grant_action RAISES on a word with no reader, which is the discipline this gap sits behind. Missing is a GRANTABLE word plus its reader for a move between two squares of a zone, and c.grant_action has no way to scope the grant to standing inside one.

actions.recharge(bonus=).why: actions.recharge is rng.roll('1d6').total >= p.recharge with no _mods lookup on either side

actions.recharge(disadvantage=).why: actions.recharge rolls world.rng.roll("1d6") flat and consults no modifier of any kind. c.reroll_attack(keep="worst") and c.damage_disadvantage are the two rolls that do have this and neither reaches a recharge. Wants engine work -- and the row is right that a bonus hook (what m2555a4 wants) would not spell "roll twice, keep the lower", so this is two shapes of one hole.

actions.shed_light().why: c.light(radius, on=, until=) plus c.endable(hold, cost=FREE) write the printed sentence exactly. What is missing is somewhere to OFFER it as a minor action: actions.GRANTABLE is ten words and holds none for light, and c.grant_action raises on a word with no reader. Wants engine actions.GRANTABLE plus its reader, or content (a granted minor-action row via c.grant_row).

actions.stand_up_cost.why: actions._recovery builds costs = {MOVE} | _granted(..., 'stand'), so grant_action can only add a cheaper entry and the MOVE floor is unconditional

actions.teleport_at_will().why: No teleport action kind exists in actions.legal (only policy/doctrine.py names the word, for move-step scoring). c.shift_as grants a shift at a different cost and c.grant_action raises on an unknown word. Wants a new kind in actions.legal, a GRANTABLE word and reader (the move_zone precedent, #583), AND a policy term -- drivers.kinds_named reds a kind with no term.

actions.touch().why: A new action kind in actions.legal. The 36 kinds it emits hold nothing of the sort. OWES A POLICY TERM (drivers.kinds_named).

affliction.tick(contagious=).why: tick walks each sheet's OWN sheet.afflictions and has no way to write onto another sheet; x5_66's clause is a check made by SOMEBODY ELSE, at THEIR next extended rest, against a DC the stage sets (14/14/20). Nothing in the tree spreads an affliction sideways through the party, and the row is right that Cast is the wrong layer -- a board has no eight hours on it.

affliction.tick(dies=).why: story/affliction.py::tick has exactly three outcomes (improves/worsens/holds) and clamps a worsening at worst(got); nothing kills at the final stage. Sheet.down, Sheet.stabilise, Party.bury and Campaign.bury exist for a BOARD death, so the pieces for removing the character are there -- the tick cannot reach them, and x5_18/x5_66/x5_81 also need something stood up in its place.

affliction.tick(fatal=).why: story/affliction.py caps a worsening stage at min(stage + 1, worst(got)); nothing can say that passing the last stage kills. The data is not there either: the disease table has no per-stage column and x5_91's two exceptions sit only in the prose spec. c.kill exists but tick runs on Sheets at an extended rest with no world. Wants ETL plus story.

affliction.tick(no_improve=).why: story/affliction.py tick makes one three-way comparison for every stage of every disease and Printed carries no per-stage data at all (ref, level, skill, two DCs, a stage COUNT). Wants a per-stage exception on Printed fed from a disease column, consulted in tick. Nothing else in the tree holds stage-level rules.

affliction.tick(rest_choice=).why: Nothing in story/ asks the party anything at a rest: tick rolls and compares, and refused() declines every decision outright (it already refuses one disease for naming a CHOICE of skills). The clause is a choice between two resources, so it needs a decision point at the extended rest plus a record of the alternative cost.

affliction.tick(rest_damage=).why: story.affliction.tick(party, seed) rolls one check and moves the stage; it never touches Sheet.hp, and an x5_ body only runs on a board via turns.arm_afflictions, so there is no extended-rest payout hook at all. Sheet.hp/max_hp already exist, so the state is there. dies= is correctly a second symbol.

by_ref().found: nothing for these two rows (build._label_refs / _cross_reference_rest exist but did not fire)
by_ref().why: Checked the built item_block specs: i3525x1 carries no power ref at all and i2801p1 carries only cf: class-feature refs, never the channel-divinity row it names. The ETL name-to-ref swap machinery is extensive and works elsewhere, but for these two the name stayed prose, which is the one thing this project may not look up.

c.ability_bonus().why: c.str_mod and its five siblings return self.stats.mod(Ability.X) with no Mods consulted anywhere on the path, so there is no modifier hook to add to -- i2814x1's note is accurate. c.bonus's `what` is attack, damage, save, speed or a defence and refuses anything else.

c.ability_check(purpose=).why: skills.ability_check announces a SkillCheck under an ability:str key with neither a subject nor a purpose, so a bonus would pay on every such check

c.act_after_charge().why: c.extra_action raises the turn's budget and announces ActionGranted, which is the thing m5854a0 wants and which it did not consider - it reasoned only about handing a zeroed slot back. I would check where actions.perform zeroes the slots relative to the charge row's own resolution emit, since the row's objection is purely one of ordering.

c.action_point(gain=False).why: c.action_point always calls extra_action and c.grant_action_point refuses count<=0; nothing decrements without handing the action over

c.active_vestige().why: c.build records which leg the warlock took and a labelled c.effect plus c.lingers_label is the general "hold and read arbitrary named state" door, with c.endable for the mid-fight switch. What I could not confirm is where the *set* of two remnants is recorded - that is the same chargen sub-choice shape as chargen.race_choice(), and whether a hold laid at a rest survives into a fight.

c.add_keyword().why: adds a keyword to this creature's copy of a named row, read via keywords_of; unconfirmed the free action resolves before the triggering attack reads its keywords

c.add_target(pending=).why: c.add_target reaches the outer use only via dsl.running_below, and _RUNNING.append happens after cast.used() emits PowerUsed, whose targets is a copy

c.advantage_on_roll().why: c.gains_advantage lays the attacker-side Mod that query.has_combat_advantage reads, and its sibling c.grants_advantage already has the spend-once machinery, so p11750/p12339 look one `once=` short. f631b and f2468 are a different half - a banked d20 reroll - and would want c.arm_trigger plus keep="best". I would check whether once= can be added to gains_advantage's Mod.

c.aim(at=).why: the origin is validated against dsl.aim_points before the body runs and c.origin is read-only; no header field narrows the aim

c.alchemical().why: i476x1's 'an alchemical item is not a thing the engine carries' is too strong: the category is a real column, the blocks are declared rows and i3320p1/i3479p1 play, so gating a bonus on ctx['power'] being one of them is reachable. i465p1 is the genuine half -- spending an item needs a consumable inventory, and Gear carries weapons, armour, a shield and a stowed set of weapon refs, nothing else.

c.alignment().why: i3282p1 and f1351 both want 'against evil creatures' and no component records an alignment -- the only occurrence in the ETL is etl/feat._KINDS classifying the *word* in a prerequisite line. f1351 also needs how much a modifier contributed to a roll already made, which is c.amplify_bonus's gap.

c.allies_in_area().why: The attack context carries attacker/target/power and not the area that was struck, so there is nothing to ask who else stands inside a burst. No candidate scored at all.

c.altitude_limit().why: m4737a3 is accurate: `c.hover` holds a creature up and `c.rise` puts it there, and neither refuses to go further. No field caps a height, so there is no half of this row to write.

c.amount_for('m305').why: both verbs exist and fit; the whole blocker is a one-line read in m305a0's body, which hands its aura damage out bare. No engine work at all

c.amplify_bonus().why: i1986p1, i2633x1 and f1398 each reach for a modifier *somebody else laid* -- 'both the effect and the size of the penalty are locals in its closure', 'nothing reaches a stored modifier' -- and Mods holds no handle a second row can find. feats.rogue_b.f810 deepens only its own penalty, by re-laying it.

c.any_size_manoeuvre(within=).why: Cast._manoeuvrable short-circuits on lingers_label(_ANY_SIZE), a binary waiver with nowhere to carry a ceiling

c.appears_unbloodied().why: c.bloodied reads Health directly and no modifier key in the engine's ~45 reads touches bloodied state

c.area_origin().why: cast_from holds a borrowed origin for a duration and measured_from honours it for ranged, area_burst and wall ranges, with the on-board-and-in-sight proviso -- so i1531p1's burst centred on the struck ally is writable today. Not run down: measured_from skips melee, so check what range kind p11769's stance is about.

c.as_basic(at_will=).why: as_basic files the offer under the window that hands the swing out -- window="ranged" is a granted ranged basic -- and dsl.basic_options drops rows the character does not possess at the moment of the swing rather than at arming. That makes the card's outcome reachable without any interrupt: the at-will is offered in place of the basic before it is declared. f987's docstring already relies on this. _spend_once is the per-encounter limit.

c.as_basic(ranged).why: the window machinery exists on both sides and Powers.ranged is the ranged basic; unconfirmed whether p7442 may be given a window name of its own

c.as_basic(spent=True).why: dsl.basic_options runs every stand-in through usable(), which refuses a spent encounter power, and nothing is past it

c.as_melee(ref).why: c.as_ranged holds a per-creature, per-duration override of a row's reach and f1239 says the second half (c.as_basic) already works, so the holder for the mirror plausibly exists. I would check whether as_ranged's key can be laid the other way, given its note that it renders "as the distance and nothing else" because _is_ranged reads the printed range line.

c.as_ranged(ref).why: c.as_ranged IS that bonus with a kind gate, and dsl._stretched gets a ctx carrying power, so when= is the ref filter. Six rows write it by hand

c.as_weapon(base=).why: i553p1 says 'the base item is a column and no body swaps it', but a Weapon is built from the weapon table by loader and Gear.weapons is an ordinary list, so taking the other base weapon's dice, reach and group means swapping the entry rather than adding a field. Same unchecked risk as Weapon.proficiency -- whether anything holds the old object.

c.as_weapon(enhancement=).why: Weapon is a plain non-frozen dataclass and content already mutates sibling fields on a weapon in Gear.weapons in place

c.as_weapon(natural=).why: p14205 says 'the bite is a weapon with its own proficiency and damage die and nothing can make one'; as_weapon takes damage=, group=, proficiency=, hands= and properties= and appends the profile to Gear.weapons. What is left is a tag for a natural weapon, not the ability to mint one.

c.attacked_this_round().why: nothing records who a creature swung at; the nearest, c.hit_this_turn(), is itself open and differs on both axes

c.attacks_with(ability=).found: c.rolls_with(ref, ability), read by Attack.ability_for before the header
c.attacks_with(ability=).why: `c.rolls_with` exists for exactly this sentence -- 'make a named row attack with a different ability', recorded against the creature because the ability is header data -- and `ability_for` reads it *before* the header. cf:warlord-marshal-f0 refuses on the grounds that `basic.RANGED` fixes the ability in its own header 'where no modifier can reach it', which is the problem `rolls_with` was written to solve.

c.augment_area().why: Targets are chosen before a row's body runs, so a widening applied from inside the body arrives after the area was measured -- the augment cannot reach it. A zone's squares are frozen when laid and a wall's length with them, so the second row has no handle either.

c.augment_free().why: c.spend_points is the only route into an augment and the card pays for one with something else. Nothing else in the corpus scores for it.

c.aura(difficult=).why: The helper's own docstring states the workaround -- 'c.aura has no difficult= of its own ... so the workaround is to create the aura and then flip the field by hand' -- and one row already uses it. Nine rows are marked blocked while a working route sits in the tree.

c.aura(shrinks=).why: resize_aura changes a standing aura's radius in place and announces it, with cap= for a printed ceiling - so "c.aura has no shrinking radius" is stale. m4244a2 stays refused on its compendium.attack_defence defect, which is the real blocker on that card.

c.aura_effect().why: documented as hold something on whoever stands in a zone and take it back; unconfirmed only that it is private, so what is owed is a public door rather than a mechanism

c.auto_save(against=).why: That helper watches SavingThrow and sets ev.saved = True for a throw whose `against` carries the printed words, and a live row calls it at armour.py:708. m6671a0's 'there is no verb for forcing one to pass' is stale; for slowing and immobilizing it is better read off the standing effect's conditions, the way items.arms._my_save_against_hold does.

c.bank_reroll().why: Every reroll verb acts on the roll in c.trigger; p16455 needs an unspent reroll held over a window and spent on a later roll, and no component stores one.

c.basic(half_on_miss=).why: unconfirmed whether rebuilding the basic's damage outside its body is acceptable; c.hit(half=True) needs the calling row to declare its own damage line

c.basic(harmless=).why: `c.basic` delegates to `dsl.use` of whichever row the creature's basic attack actually is, so its damage cannot be suppressed from the caller. i2019p1 also needs one attack roll compared against another, which nothing does, and names `c.cancel` as unavailable because the printed action is a reaction.

c.basic(with_=).why: c.basic resolves Powers.basic through use() and takes no weapon; hand= exists only on c.strike/c.attack, and i1261x1 files the claw stowed

c.basic_ability().found: c.rolls_with (read by Attack.ability_for before the header), Powers.basic, Powers.rolls
c.basic_ability().why: rolls_with records the swap against the creature rather than the row, for exactly the reason these rows give, and a basic attack is an ordinary ref held in Powers.basic -- so 'use a different modifier for melee basic attacks' is that call aimed at the creature's own basic row.

c.beast_attacks().why: The clause needs the beast to swing and the companion never takes a turn (#212), so a rider paying out on its hit would be a clause with no case. The row reasons this out and marks rather than writes, which is the right call.

c.become(ref=).why: Nothing swaps which stat block drives a creature mid-fight: c.form changes shape and modifiers, query.stat_block only reads. m1825a3 is refused downstream of m1825a2 for the same reason.

c.best_ability().why: Pick.HIGHEST is documented as the header spelling of "Highest ability modifier vs. Will" and resolves per caster in Attack.ability_for, which also takes a plain tuple and returns max(key=stats.mod) (dsl.py:579). i1066p1's "nothing answers whichever of mine is largest. Fifty-four rows print the phrase" is stale for all of them.

c.blocks_entry().why: Occupancy already refuses both walking and teleporting into a creature's square -- `fits()` rejects an occupied square unless the caller passes `share=True` -- so m6404a1 and m5624a1 both say the printed absolute line adds nothing today. Check whether `c.phasing` or any `share=True` caller can breach it; if not, these rows are writable as confirmations the way `cf:fighter-weaponmaster-f3s0` writes a gate that is false today.

c.blocks_occupancy().why: m6405a1 records its own search ('grep -n "def blocks_occupancy" cast.py' and vocab.py --brief both empty) and the engine agrees: movement._occupied only asks whether the *occupant* shares its space, and c.shares_space grants the opposite. Nothing names a square unenterable against phasing or insubstantial movement.

c.bonded().why: No attunement model: Relation has ten members and none is creature-to-item. Item.was records whose a DROPPED WEAPON was and c.recall_weapon is literally the "bonded weapon" sentence built on it, but there is no rest-established persistent bond and nothing gates an item's powers on one. Wants a component field plus a requires-readable reader; the bonding is out of combat, so chargen/story has to set it.

c.bonded_to(penalty=).why: Two halves, neither present. Nothing records a creature's bond to a HELD weapon -- Item.was records whose a DROPPED weapon was, and c.disarm is its only writer. And no verb lays a penalty keyed on "whoever is wielding this and is not its owner". Wants a recorded bond plus a Cast verb.

c.bonus('save:death').why: c.bonus("save", -2, on=victim, when=lambda ctx: ctx.get("label") == "death"). turns._death_saves reads mods.total("save", {... "label": "death" ...}); TWO live content precedents spell the gate exactly that way (feats/ranger_b.py:1015, feats/general_l.py:2648). m2295a1's "nothing holds a modifier the death save reads" is STALE.

c.bonus(against=).why: Nothing PREDICTS what a power's body will apply. c.bonus(when=) already takes an arbitrary attack-context predicate, so the parameter is not the gap -- the ctx carries the power ref, opportunity, ranged, dtype and NO STATEMENT of the conditions the body will impose. c.pass_on is the near-miss and it REACTS, arming a watch for conditions as they land, which is useless to a defence consulted at to-hit time. Wants the conditions a row imposes as HEADER data (dsl.Power plus an ETL field) plus a ctx key.

c.bonus(any_roll=).why: c.bonus(once=True) banks a one-shot for one kind of roll and c.boost_roll adds to a roll already made; nothing banks one any of four rolls may spend

c.bonus(clock=).why: could not confirm the enemy's first TurnEnd reads as 'end of its next turn' when the row fires during that enemy's turn

c.bonus(compute=).why: Mod carries `roll: Callable[[], int] | None`, 'called once per time the modifier is read, which is once per roll'. i1623p1 needs the enemy count recomputed at each swing, which is that callable; c.bonus only exposes it as a `dice` string, so the gap is the Cast door and not the mechanism.

c.bonus(ends_with=).why: SavingThrow carries actor/against/saved and f305b matches str(eff) against ev.against to recover the hold

c.bonus(instead=).why: Bus.emit runs BEFORE/resolve/AFTER and skills.check builds its CheckResult after AFTER returns; unconfirmed this is a supported route, no row overrides a total this way

c.bonus(multiply=).why: `c.change_amount(ref, n)` sets a named mechanic's number outright rather than adding, and `c.amount_for(ref, default)` is the read -- which is the shape a doubling needs. Check whether a weapon's two range thresholds can be named mechanics that way; p10744's second half (the weapon is unknown when the stance is taken) looks genuinely open either way.

c.bonus(of_ref=).why: change_amount is exactly this but warns a row must read it to be changed; unconfirmed m1031a4 can be re-pointed to lay its bonus through c.amount_for

c.bonus(per_die=).found: nothing (c.change_dice and c.weapon_dice are the near misses the row already ruled out)
c.bonus(per_die=).why: A modifier is laid against a roll's total and nothing scales with how many dice made it, so '-2 to each die of damage' has no hook; f763 and f2766 want the same arithmetic from the other direction. The row's note is the best evidence and it has already been re-aimed twice.

c.bonus(regeneration).why: change_amount is the verb for raising a number another mechanic hands out, and regeneration granted by a named row (p2483, which is declared) is that shape. Not run down: the contract requires the granting row to read amount_for, so p2483 would have to be rewritten -- and this row's other half, Healed.regeneration, is a real gap either way.

c.bonus(retype=).why: Both existing retypes touch the damage a row rolls itself; resolve.deal_damage splits a blow into typed parts and only parts[0] is reachable from the event, so the part a modifier contributed cannot be recoloured. f1639's rider rolls no damage of its own at all.

c.bonus(skill=).why: escape.attempt reads the escape modifier with ctx {actor, holder, skill}, so when= narrows it exactly as the card prints

c.bonus(while_adjacent=).why: c.aura returns a zone id, c.grants_in carries a modifier for as long as you stand in it, and _while_inside takes the hold back on ZoneExited

c.bonus_feat().found: build._named_feats, and the refs are already in data/game.db
c.bonus_feat().why: Queried class_feature: cf:ranger-f0s0's spec now carries f127 and cf:ranger-f0s4's carries f171, both declared rows. build._named_feats' docstring records the fix -- names sitting at the *head* of a run, 'three of them a ranger leg', each granting a feat whose ref already existed. Both markers are stale; write them the way cf:ranger-f0s3 writes f172.

c.boost_attack().why: m1796a3 says 'an attack roll or a saving throw can only be rerolled whole'; c.boost_roll's own docstring is 'add to the triggering roll without rolling it again', and its body handles result.total for attack and ev.bonus/ev.saved for a save. Caveat: boost_roll reads c.trigger, so i1186p1 (a daily minor with no trigger) stays blocked.

c.boost_check(ability=).why: skills.ability_check announces a SkillCheck under key ability:<name>, so m3676a4's unfiltered SkillCheck trigger already fires on an ability check

c.boost_roll(extra=).why: p6186 reads its die through c.dice_for and hands the skill and which power rolled it over in the context, precisely so a feat can narrow - and f1836 (general_k.py:608) already swaps that die with a gate on the kind of roll. f718's and i2295x1's "+1 to the d6 p6186 itself rolls, only for an arcane/divine power" is the same call with a different die and a different gate.

c.boost_roll(kind_of_bonus=).why: c.boost_roll's kind is WHICH ROLL (attack/save/check) and is a refusal filter, not a bonus type -- its own docstring says so. It adds to the total and emits Boosted; no Mod is laid, so there is no bonus type and the non-stacking rule cannot see it. c.bonus(kind=, stacks=) carries that discipline but is summed before the die. Wants a bonus-type argument Mods.total's non-stacking pass can see.

c.boost_save().why: That helper adds to the announced SavingThrow and rewrites ev.saved ('the total is rewritten here the way SkillCheck is rewritten by c.boost_check') and a live row calls it at waist.py:417 -- which is exactly the twin i1354p1's docstring asks for. m1796a3's attack-roll branch is also stale: c.boost_roll adds to a roll already made (#495).

c.borrow_row(seen=).why: that helper is the seen-powers ledger exactly -- it walks bus.log for PowerUsed against c.borrowed_rows -- and c.borrow_row(among=) takes the refs it returns

c.borrow_row(source=).found: The row's stated blocker is STALE: chargen
c.borrow_row(source=).why: The row's stated blocker is STALE: chargen.power_source(cls) exists (#1094) and reads class.power, which holds divine|martial|arcane|primal|psionic|shadow for all 26 classes -- and selecting divine returns exactly the five classes f1552's docstring enumerates. What is left is ONE PARAMETER: c.borrow_row filters p.cls == cls and needs power_source(p.cls) == source with the caster's own class excluded. among= is also assemblable today.

c.brutal().why: exactly reroll each damage die under an exclusive threshold individually, read inside _roll_damage, and it takes on=/until=

c.burns(condition=).why: that helper holds several effects on whoever is in a zone and takes them back on exit; the hazard can stand and the condition be laid beside it

c.can_hear().why: There is no sound model anywhere: no hearing key beside the darkvision/low_light/blindsight/tremorsense set that query.sees_in reads, and no distance verb for it. All three rows fall back to sight and say so.

c.cannot_act(during=).found: Budget.immediate_round / Budget.opportunity_turn, flipped from a watcher -- m193a3's precedent
c.cannot_act(during=).why: During somebody else's turn the only actions a creature has are immediates and opportunities, and both are gated on those two stamps in Encounter.can_spend; m193a3 already writes one from content. So p16673's bar can be laid by stamping them at the caster's TurnStart and clearing at TurnEnd, which is narrower than dazed or stunned, as the row asks.

c.cannot_attack(except_=).why: p14462 writes the identical bar as a cancelling AttackDeclared listener and its docstring says c.cannot_attack is too coarse

c.cannot_attack(opportunity=).why: c.cannot_attack already refuses at AttackDeclared in the BEFORE window, and resolve sets `announced.opportunity = opportunity` on that very event -- _was_opportunity reads it with getattr today. Narrowing is a gate on a flag already on the event the verb reads.

c.cannot_attack(when=).why: this same row already uses _until_escape two lines earlier to give the burn the grab's lifetime

c.cannot_hide().found: nothing (c.no_walk / c.cannot_shift / c.cannot_attack are the precedent family)
c.cannot_hide().why: `actions._hiding` is the single place a hide is offered and it consults only cover, concealment and `hidden_from` -- no effect can refuse one, which is exactly m6644a2's reading that every hide method stops at doing or reading a hide. The verb would be new, though `c.no_walk`/`c.cannot_shift` show the shape.

c.cannot_mark().why: relations.set refuses a mark when immune_to says so and the gate gets source; unconfirmed because it must be laid on each enemy at arm time, so it misses later arrivals

c.cannot_opportunity().why: already writes this sentence, subscribing to OpportunityWindow at Window.BEFORE and cancelling when ev.actor is the held creature

c.cannot_speak().why: the 24-condition vocabulary has no entry for speech and no reader would consult one

c.cannot_stand().why: its docstring reads: held is for 'falls prone and cannot stand up until ...', which is a second, shorter clock on top of the first

c.carries().why: carried-when-the-mount-moves works; c.ride makes the caster the rider and has no by= to make the target one

c.carrying(thing).why: the component docstring says by is whoever is holding or controlling it, and query.scenery already reads it for loose=. c.carrying is the wrong reader, not a missing one

c.cast_from(ref=).why: Cast.cast_from(who, on=, until=) does the whole effect; only the ref= narrowing is absent. Five sibling verbs already carry exactly that narrowing. c.strike(from_=) is the one-swing spelling and does not reach a future use.

c.cast_through().why: The engine knows what a power was cast through only for the enhancement bonus it lends. Nothing substitutes a held object's range and proficiency for the power's own, which is the whole of this row.

c.change_amount(compute=).why: Cast.change_amount(ref, amount: int, *, on, until, when) stores (amount, when). Mod.roll: Callable[[], int] | None is the precedent one store over, and even that takes no ctx where this needs one (count adjacent enemies at the swing). Wants engine cast.change_amount plus c.amount_for's read.

c.change_beneficiary().why: Cast.pre_empt(ref, what, clause) paired with Cast.instead_of is the "one row replaces a named clause of another row" facility; p3773's body picks mates[0] off a local list and would wrap that pick in c.instead_of. Per content/CLAUDE.md #550 the preferred shape is simpler still: write the clause into p3773's body gated on c.feat("f1027").

c.change_distance(ref, n).why: extend_move is literally 'make a named row move you further' keyed by ref, entries add so a negative shortens. Both rows say the hold is that cf:barbarian-f1s3 and cf:rogue-scoundrel-f1s2 hard-code their numbers -- which extend_move's docstring names as the content-side bug ('a row must read it to be changed, with squares_for').

c.charge_at(at=).why: The charge works and square selection exists everywhere else (c.shift(to=), c.teleport(to=), world.reachable_squares), but neither c.charge_at(victim, ref, who) nor c.run_at(victim, who) threads a destination, so nothing today names the walk-in square. Not run down: whether a body can walk by hand and then swing with the charge flag set, which would make this writable without a kwarg.

c.charge_target().why: actions._charging computes speed once before the per-foe loop picks a target, and query.speed's ctx is {'charge': True} and nothing else so far

c.charge_with().why: c.as_basic is "you can use <this row> in place of a melee basic attack" filed under the window that hands the swing out, and "charge" is one of its four windows; actions._charges feeds its swings from basic_options(world, actor, "charge"). So the swap is made before the charge resolves, which is i2088p2's whole objection to c.charge_at.

c.charges().found: Powers.per_day with c.per_day_left / c.spend_per_day, and Powers.used/times(ref)
c.charges().why: i2017p1 says 'an item with a pool of its own is not a thing Magic carries', but a counted, daily-refreshed pool keyed by ref exists and content calls it (features/martial_leaders: 'the gap was the bridge, not the counter'). What I did not run down: whether one pool can be shared by an item's several blocks, and what a non-daily recharge would hang on.

c.choose(before_damage=).why: c.choose exists but is only ever called from inside a body; f1858 needs a question put to the holder at a moment -- before the damage dice are rolled -- that nothing offers. Keyword.RAGE already closed the other half of this row.

c.chosen_weapon_group().found: Build.choices (a free-form set[str]) read by c.build, Gear.counts_as, feats.general_o._group
c.chosen_weapon_group().why: `BuildState.choices` is an extensible string set already carrying `race:<ref>`, `element:<x>` and `primary:<x>`, and `c.build(word)` is a plain membership test -- the same shape as the `race:<ref>` mis-mark already found. Groups are a column `_group` asks about and `Gear.counts_as` already records proficiency waivers, so 'two weapons this character picked' needs a `weapon:<group>` entry, not new machinery.

c.class_feature().found: cf: rows are ordinary @power rows and emit PowerUsed; build._features, build._sub_features
c.class_feature().why: A class feature that has a `cf:` row announces itself like any other row, so the absence is narrower than the symbol: i1942x1/p1's feature has no `cf:` row at all and f3621/f3626/f3645 name features only in prose. Check the same thing `spec.feature_ref()` needs -- which features `etl.build._features` actually imports -- and note that a mid-fight *invocation* of a passive feature has no moment even when the row exists.

c.clear_shrouds().why: Shrouds lives on the caster keyed to one victim and c.shroud resets it on re-aim, so the old victim's count is already 0 -- satisfied by construction

c.collide().why: movement.forced walks _line and stops at the first square it cannot enter, so the impact square is findable; unconfirmed because nothing picks a random direction or pays the damage

c.combined_attack().why: m3842a3 and f3797 both want one attack rolled on behalf of several creatures, with the others paying for it. `c.use_power`, `c.grant_attack` and `c.aid_attack` each move one creature's swing; nothing pools several into a single roll.

c.conceal(against=).why: Cast.penalty("attack", 2, on=victim, until=...). m1505a1 (level 5, UNMARKED) models the identical printed sentence "all creatures have concealment against it" that way and argues it: concealment's whole effect is -2 to whoever is looking, so a penalty on the target says it exactly; monsters/level_12/lurkers_sa._total_concealment_from is the -5 form with a when=ctx["target"] gate. CAVEAT the precedent states: a penalty ADDS to real cover where the rule takes the larger.

c.conceal(except_for=).why: c.see_unseen already loops one HIDDEN_FROM per onlooker; unconfirmed whether being HIDDEN_FROM bars targeting outright or only grants combat advantage

c.conceal(from_light=).why: Light is on the board per square and per looker, so reading the square being left and laying a carried `c.conceal(until=)` is writable now; conceal even takes a context predicate. f3067b's 'lighting is not on the board' predates the light model.

c.conceal(square=).why: cast.py:8677 documents obscured=Light.DIM as exactly 'lightly obscured' on the zone this row already lays; c.conceal_in is the per-creature sibling

c.conceal_from().why: level_12.lurkers_sa._total_concealment_from states the model -- the engine holds no concealment state and the whole of what it does is take five off whoever is looking

c.conceal_in(entirely=).why: containment is askable as set(pos.squares) <= area; unconfirmed a hand-rolled zone pair catches half-in to fully-in without crossing a boundary

c.conceal_in(kind=).why: c.conceal_in takes only a zone, a side word and total; Cast._while_inside is private so content cannot pass a type filter

c.concealment_cap(within=, when=).why: Engine: a modifier key, a query reader, and one branch in resolve.attack. Confirmed the row's reading: resolve.py:217 is `if from_concealment <= concealment_waived(...): from_concealment = 0` -- a THRESHOLD, so waiving at PARTIAL leaves total concealment untouched and waiving at SUPERIOR clears it. Neither is "-5 becomes -2"; that needs a min() against a cap read after the waiver.

c.condition(cannot_approach=).why: c.leash is the only direction-aware restriction and applies as a maximum; four sibling rows name this gap c.cannot_approach(), which is the spelling to use

c.condition(ends_with_check=).why: c.endable(effect, cost, then=) sets Effect.drop_cost, and actions.legal offers a drop to the effect's OWNER -- so the action-cost half and the offer site exist. Missing: a DC'd skill check gating the drop, and allowing an ADJACENT ALLY to be the one offered it. The gap is on Effect/actions.legal/skills.check, A LAYER BELOW the c.condition parameter the symbol names.

c.condition(when=).why: weakened is a bare Condition with no modifier key behind it, so unlike c.bonus there is no gate-bearing mod to carve an ally out of

c.conjuration_hp().why: c.wall is the one map object given hit points where c.conjure spawns no Health; unconfirmed whether a wall can also carry the speed, the opportunity bite and the pass-through clause

c.conjure(defences=).why: Read the body: conjure spawns Ident, Position, Movement and Conjuration and no Health or Defences, so the thing is on the board and targetable but cannot be hit for damage or destroyed. world.spawn takes components, so defences are additive -- what has no precedent at all is m1659a5's other half, routing a hit on the object into a creature's Health.

c.conjure(hp=).why: with hp the wall spawns a Barrier carrying Health so it can be attacked, c.barrier hands it back, and solid=False keeps the square out of Grid.blocking

c.conjure(porous=).why: c.wall(solid=) and Grid.blocking stop everyone alike, c.zone(exempt=) exempts only from sight-blocking, and c.phasing would let an ally through everything

c.conjure(side=).why: solid= blocks everybody and Zone.exempt is sight-only; its docstring says a set of ids cannot waive passage for one side and such rows keep their markers

c.conjure_weapon().why: c.as_weapon grants damage, group, proficiency, properties and hands for a duration and c.conjure makes an entity, so the shape is largely there. What I did not confirm is whether as_weapon can carry the enhancement bonus and critical die p15895 says are the weapon's own columns - if it can, this is one call.

c.considered_bloodied().why: Health.bloodied is a derived property (hp <= max_hp // 2) with no override anywhere, and resolve/query read it directly -- so i691p1's 'bloodied for all purposes without losing hit points' has nothing to pretend with, exactly as it says.

c.consume().why: that is the engine's one-shot model; unconfirmed a character's own item block exists as an Item entity to spend down

c.consume_item().found: engine/ammunition.py, Item(uses=, spend=), c.give, actions._spending, Ammo.kind
c.consume_item().why: The spend machinery exists end to end: `c.give` spawns a one-shot with charges, `actions._spending` offers it, and ammunition is a modelled consumable whose ref lands on all four attack events. What is missing is that neither `chargen` nor `story` ever deals a character an `Item` or any `Ammo` -- check there before building a verb.

c.counts_as(enhancement=).why: unconfirmed whether a Mods bonus reaches an implement attack the way _enhancement_of does, since that number never passes through Mods

c.counts_as(feat=).why: The existing verb is read by query.wielding and answers only about what is in hand; c.feat(ref) has no writer. m4027a4 also reports its brief names the feat by this row's own ref, so there would be nothing to point a verb at.

c.counts_as(kind=).why: `c.set_origin` writes type/origin words onto a creature as labelled effects that `kinds_of` (and so `c.is_kind`) reads back, and `instead_of=` even takes a word off -- which is most of what f1509/f1511 ask. The residual is that the printed line applies for one attacker only, and writing it globally would be stronger than the card; check whether the origin label can be read through a `when=` gate on the asking row.

c.counts_as(property=).found: c.weapon_dice (writes the per-character `replace(w)` copies in Gear.weapons), feats.fighter_c._with_property, Cast._high_crit
c.counts_as(property=).why: weapon_dice already edits one character's own copy of a weapon and needs no reader, which is the exact mechanism these rows want for `Weapon.properties`; `_high_crit` and `_with_property` already read the field. f1277's three clauses (dice, properties, group, range) are the same write on the same object. The three symbols c.make_thrown(), c.weapon_range() and c.counts_as(property=) are ONE mechanism over 10 distinct rows -- f1841/f1843 carry two of them and f1277 carries two. #643.

c.counts_as(usage=).why: Neither near-miss is this. c.counts_as(satisfies, holding=, kind=, keyword=) is about the CREATURE; c.counts_as_keyword retypes a ROW's keyword only. Nothing says "treat this row as a different usage or class". Wants a Powers-level override plus the readers that filter by usage/cls. NOTE f2034's real hold is its other symbol cf:wizard-arcanist-f0c1, a ref with no row, so this one is secondary either way.

c.counts_as_kind().why: lays origin:<word> as a labelled effect that query.kinds_of reads back explicitly, and dsl.candidates asks that same reader

c.coup_de_grace(basic=True).why: sets ev.result.critical = True on the live Hit, which is the automatic critical the row says cannot be had; the row already calls c.maximise without the flag

c.coup_de_grace(bonus=).why: the attack ctx already carries which named swing this is, and c.coup_de_grace is the one caller tagging nothing; unconfirmed whether as_ is the intended carrier for a finisher

c.cover().why: the exact channel c.cover_in lays; query.cover_between takes the larger of the geometric trace and a carried cover modifier

c.cover(when=).why: query._carried_cover reads mods.total('cover', {}) with an empty ctx, so a when= can never see the attacker or the power

c.cover_from().found: c.conceal (the self-side precedent), c.cover_in (the zone-side writer), query.cover_between, feats.warlord_b._covering
c.cover_from().why: RE-JUDGED, and it is THREE gaps rather than the one this entry named. The old verdict said 'what is missing is a Cast door, not a mechanism' over query.cover_between -- true of exactly one of the five rows. Read the cards: (1) GRANT cover to yourself, gated on a circumstance -- f3527 'when in a square of difficult terrain, you gain partial cover against ranged attacks', f3701 'you gain partial cover from ranged and area attacks', p16434 'you gain partial cover while adjacent to a square of blocking terrain'. That is a WRITER and cover_between is a reader. c.conceal is the exact precedent -- the self-side sibling of c.conceal_in, as a self-side c.cover would be of c.cover_in. (2) READ whether I have cover -- f1296's 'if you move into an obscured space or gain cover before making a ranged attack'. This is the one the old verdict fits. (3) ATTRIBUTE cover to the creatures providing it -- i778x1's 'each enemy granting your target cover takes damage'. warlord_b._covering reportedly already asks this, so it may be writable alone. A marker names one gap, so these five want three symbols.

c.cover_in.why: IT EXISTS -- c.cover_in(zone, *, side="team", when=), listed in docs/symbols/modifiers.md. It is in the worklist only because blocked._wants_of mined it out of p13318:augment1's PROSE, where the entry cites it as a thing that ALREADY exists. A parse artifact, not a gap.

c.crawl().why: MoveStart.kind_ has six words -- walk, shift, teleport, push, pull, slide -- and crawling is not one of them, so there is no half speed to raise and no move to exempt from provoking.

c.crit_damage().found: c.total(what, on, ctx); "crit_damage" is an ordinary Mods key at resolve.py:959
c.crit_damage().why: `resolve.deal_damage` sums the crit rider with `_split_mods(world, source, "crit_damage", dmg_ctx)` -- a normal modifier key -- and `c.total("crit_damage", on=..., ctx=...)` is the general reader for exactly that. i709p1's claim that 'nothing outside that branch can ask for the total' is wrong.

c.curse_damage().why: c.reroll_ones' docstring names "the curse damage" as exactly what its `ref=` narrows to, f2764 says extra_damage reads its die through c.dice_for now, and warlock_f1c11 already pays curse damage inline with c.damage - so f1124/f2036/f2760 are writable today. Only the once-a-round latch is left, and that is c.extra_damage(applies=).

c.damage(ignore_temp_hp=).why: resolve.deal_damage absorbs health.temp unconditionally at the point of application, and unpreventable=True short-circuits only resistance, immunity and vulnerability

c.damage_disadvantage(against=).why: The rows' stated reason is wrong: c.damage_disadvantage is 'held on the creature that rolls' and takes on=, so it already lands on somebody else. What is genuinely absent is the *attack*-roll twin as a standing modifier -- reroll_attack(keep="worst") only answers a triggering roll. Not run down: whether these two traits are about attack rolls or damage rolls, which decides the verdict outright.

c.damage_of(ref).why: CORRECTED from mis-marked. The lane0 verdict claimed dsl.REGISTRY[ref].damage.dice IS the printed damage expression, so a row could read another row's die. Measured over the set these rows actually choose from -- c.borrowed_rows, i.e. class rows, at-will, standard action, carrying an attack -- 359 rows, and ZERO carry header damage. Header damage is the MONSTER convention; a class power rolls its dice in its body via c.damage("1d8"), so REGISTRY[chosen].damage.dice is None.dice. Samples with no header damage: p10274 p10275 p10276 p11061 p12932. The roll-time route is closed too -- DamageRolled carries amount, dtype, detail, dtypes and NO dice expression -- so nothing can read the face before or during the roll. The .keywords half of the old verdict is sound (absence of Keyword.WEAPON is askable); the die is not. The three dropped=('c.damage_of(ref)',) markers on f1281b/f1283b/f1287b are correct as written. general_r.py carries a sibling symbol for the same family (DICE = ('c.change_dice()',)) and this may want grouping there.

c.damages_with(ref, ability).why: rolls_with is read by Attack.ability_for and never by damage, and the named row works its number out inside its own closure (`c.flat(3 + c.cha_mod, ...)`), so there is nothing for a swap to be read by. The row's own analysis checks out.

c.deals(add=True).why: A blow of several types at once already exists -- c.damage takes dtypes and Mod.dtype is a tuple 'because 1d6 extra cold and lightning damage is one rider of two types' -- and _typed/_retyped is a single read site returning one type. Not run down: whether this card adds a type to the attack's own dice or only to a rider, which decides whether the fix is at _typed or is one c.bonus(dtype=).

c.deals(chosen=).why: c.deals has five narrowings (from_, ref, vs_kind, through, ranged) and once=True, but NO per-blow opt-in; c.may(what, who=) and c.reshape_area(optional=) are the opt-in pattern used elsewhere, and i509x1's second need -- writing a keyword onto the converted power -- is already c.counts_as_keyword(ref, keyword). ONE SYMBOL, TWO GAPS: i509x1 wants a wielder's per-blow choice, f795 wants the retype scoped to the swing a feature GRANTED (granted_via), a different narrowing. Per content/CLAUDE.md these want different symbols.

c.deals(dtypes=).why: A blow of two types at once is a shape the pipeline very much has: four Cast verbs and the Damage header take dtypes, DamageRolled.dtypes is writable specifically so a listener can say "and" rather than "instead", and p15899 - a neighbour of a waiting row - deals cold and necrotic in one roll. Only the `deals:` label is single-valued.

c.deals(half=).why: a blow carries one DamageType or a set that is all of it at once; neither splits one blow into a radiant half and an untyped half

c.deals(like=).why: c.deals(ref=) already names one row and dsl.get(ref).damage.dtype reads that row's PRINTED type, so the simple reading is writable today.
